the damping of collective nuclear motion is dominated by particle-hole correlations and that the thermodynamic properties of nuclear matter beyond mean field are not much different from those of a mean field system.

the collective motion of nuclei is damped by particle-particle and particle-hole correlations, and that the thermodynamic properties of correlated nuclear systems differ from the ones of mean-field nuclei by a small amount.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the damping of collective motion is dominated by particle-hole correlations and that the thermodynamic properties of a nuclear system at finite excitation energy are not very sensitive to the presence of short-range correlations.

the dynamical description of nuclear collective motion in the framework of a density-matrix hierarchy is a promising tool for the description of nuclear dynamics in a broad range of excitation energies.

the inclusion of correlations beyond mean field does not change the thermodynamical behaviour of the nuclear system drastically but it changes the transport coefficients and thus the time scales of the nuclear dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inclusion of particle-hole correlations in a microscopic description of collective nuclear motion is crucial for the understanding of the damping mechanism of collective modes and for thermodynamic quantities of finite nuclei.

the inclusion of correlations in the description of collective motion beyond mean field leads to a damping of the motion that is significantly larger than the one obtained in TDHF and Vlasov approaches, and which is comparable to the results of VUU and quantum molecular dynamics.
the damping of collective motion is a non-perturbative many-body phenomenon which cannot be captured by a simple mean-field picture.
